findings: BASELINE r3: node tools/harness/boot-check.mjs PASS at start of pass. Load 1.19-5.6 on four cores.

TOOL 1 build-viability REBUILT. ctx.dispositions is now built the way Engine.seedDispositions() builds it (raw record disposition; unseeded id -> gate.js num(undefined)=0). The derived-ceiling walk is DEMOTED to record.counterfactual_race_gate, labelled COUNTERFACTUAL, and never produces a criterion verdict.

NEW MODEL: quest npc_disposition consequences (machine.js:424) are counted as a real in-play route, as a player-optimal UPPER BOUND (seed + every positive gift from every quest except the target and its mutual exclusives). A gate this bound cannot clear is a gate no play can clear.

RESULT on this tree: 0/540 viable, 540 NOT VIABLE (FAIL, not unmeasurable), exit 1. 9 quests carry a giver disposition bar no play can reach: Q-ARCH-01/dyer-sallis 0/30, Q-SOUL-02/undertaker-vaskh 0/40, Q-BLAK-01/prefect-hallow 0/20, Q-STRM-01/quartermaster-sedd 0/25, Q-LILM-01/harbourmistress-tesh 16/45, Q-SAP-01/cutter-neeth 0/40, Q-LEDG-01/factor-belliene 0/35, Q-DOCK-01/npc-porter-eeja 0/30, Q-DEEP-01/speaker-teel-ashaan 0/50. THE RECORD-LESS GIVERS ARE NOW A BUILD FAIL, not corpus debt.

WHY THE FAIL IS AIRTIGHT: for 8 of the 9 the ONLY positive npc_disposition consequence is authored on the quest the giver themself gates (circular). harbourmistress-tesh gets +8 from Q-MAG-01 and +8 from Q-MAG-20, total 16, against a required 45. And __HARNESS.npcDisposition() answers 'nobody by that name is in the world' for all nine in the RUNNING build, so Charm (sim/magic/apply.js:880) cannot reach them either.
RED, on the running engine (independent of the self-test): __HARNESS.questOffers() reports exactly nine `X disposition 0/N` clauses, one per record-less giver, matching the tool's list id for id.

GREEN, on the running engine: shadow tree (scratchpad/shadow/game) with the nine records minted at disposition 60 -> questOffers() reports ZERO disposition clauses; the tool at --data-root on the same tree reports 540/540 viable, 0 unpassable gates.

RED AGAIN on a working tree: shadow2 lowers speaker-teel-ashaan 60 -> 10. Engine: 'speaker-teel-ashaan disposition 10/50'. Tool: 1 unpassable gate, 0/540 viable. Tool and engine agree in all three states.
build-viability --self-test 18/18, including an explicit RED check, an explicit GREEN check (seed_disposition fixture), and an N-1-blocks/N-opens bar check so the FAIL is not a constant.
--signatures is now READ: 'all', a race id (walks 54 cells), or a count; an unrecognised value is a usage error. It was advertised and inert for two rounds.

TOOL 2 tools/lib/absence.mjs REBUILT. (a) needs is VALIDATED at load against the live surface AND the amendment register corpus/88-journeys/JOURNEY-CRITIC-FLEET.md, cross-checked against the running build's harness_amendments_absent; an unvalidated name refuses the run with EXIT 22 NEEDS_UNVALIDATED and NO absence verdict. (b) not_implemented[].what is PARSED AS A LIST (sentences, drop the sentences declaring something landed, split on the build's own separators, strip amendment parentheticals) - exported as parseDeclaredSystems() so a critic can run it on any string. (c) ARRIVED now requires a positive-evidence probe spec.arrived(); without one the best state available is UNCONFIRMED.

The invented needs names are gone. The register names __HARNESS.forceGC() on A-JRN9's row and getResourceRegistry() on A-JRN14's row; those are what heap-walk/leak-run/stream-audit/asset-budget now declare. The four audio reporters declare NO absent method (no amendment declares an audio surface) and rest on the live signal getWorldStats().audioMB === 0.
browser.mjs: additive handle.chromiumArgs — the exact Chromium flag list, Node-side, so the T1 gate can consult the launch flags the page cannot reach.

*** BLOCKER, NOT MINE, LANDED MID-PASS: game/src/engine.js (uncommitted, M) grew Engine._assertGiversAreVisibleToRace() at line 4686, which THROWS in _boot: '19 quest givers with no NPC record, 13 with a record and no reaction_group'. __HARNESS.ready() rejects, so EVERY browser-based tool in the tree exits 12 and boot-check FAILS. This is the same data defect build-viability measures; the assertion is correct and its owner is mid-write on the npc records. Retry boot-check.

*** THE TREE MOVED UNDER THIS PASS AND IT CHANGED THE ANSWER. Another agent landed (a) game/data/npcs/quest-givers.json with 19 minted records + reaction_group on 37 mainline records, and (b) Engine._questDispositionModel() installed on QuestEngine.dispositionModel, with QuestEngine.context().dispositions = dispositionView() running every giver through _dispositionToward() -> derivedDisposition(). THE QUEST-OFFER PATH IS NOW RACE-SENSITIVE. Round 2's model (raw seed) and round 3's first model were both correct for the tree at the moment they were written and both became wrong hours later.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TOOL: build-viability now DETECTS which offer model the build implements, from three NAMED SOURCE ANCHORS (engine.js `this.questEngine.dispositionModel =`; machine.js `_dispositionToward` consulting `this.dispositionModel`; machine.js `dispositions: this.dispositionView()`), reports the anchors it matched, and REFUSES (exit 20) when the halves disagree — a half-wired race term is the state this corpus has twice been misled by. --offer-model raw|derived forces either.

AND --cross-check: boots the game and compares the static walk's per-giver numbers against the running build's questOffers()/explainDisposition(). Result on the current tree: AGREES, 0 disagreements, model 'derived', engine refused 0 givers. This is how a tool RI-MTH06 requires to be static stays true to the world.

build-viability --self-test 20/20 on the current tree. The RED is now an INJECTED defect (unseed_givers fixture reproduces the record-less state) rather than a description of one afternoon's data, so it keeps working after the data is fixed: no_unpassable_gate FAIL 0 -> 540, givers stopping at least one signature 0 -> 3, 0 unmeasurable. Monotone seed ladder 0->540, 15->270, 30->36, 45->0, 60->0, 100->0 fail proves the NUMBER is read, not the presence of a record.

TOOL 6 perf-run REBUILT. (a) t1Verdict now takes an env {launch, pageRenderer}; launchArgAudit() reads handle.chromiumArgs NODE-SIDE, so a page claiming an RTX 4070 while this runner passed --use-angle=swiftshader is REFUSED. (b) attestation_contradicts_environment when --attest-renderer disagrees with the page. (c) fail-closed allowlist: the four TOOL-COVERAGE-R2 §3 strings (Microsoft Basic Render Driver, WebKit WebGL, Google Inc. (Google), Subzero Device) are all now REFUSED, and an unidentified vendor is refused. (d) FALSIFIABILITY PRESERVED: --t1-only --attest-renderer without --live is MANIFEST MODE which consults no environment and CAN go ADMISSIBLE, so the gate is not a constant either way; the artifact says which mode it was. --self-test 11/11 (no browser).

TOOL 8 decoupling REBUILT as a real Tier-S instrument for RI-PLT01 M6 + M7. Two declared substitutions: (1) NO F3 SCENARIO FILE EXISTS - the nearest shipped fixture is cmb-duel-infantry, declared on every run; (2) renderRateHz is a TWO-STATE quantity on the stepFrames path in mode 'harness' (core/loop.js rAF neither steps nor draws; engine.js:3212 renders once per stepFrames call when the rate is non-zero), so the tool drives the render CADENCE itself at chunk = round(60/rate) and reports the render counts per rate as the NULL CONTROL - identical render counts would mean the perturbation was never applied.

decoupling verified on the running engine: 120 steps at rate 60 -> 120 renders, at rate 0 -> 0 renders, IDENTICAL body_sha256 e389e9060b43860a, identical M7 (player_z 4.8113, camera_yaw 344.5078 - non-trivial, so M7 is not a vacuous control). --break-decoupling injects an init script making stepFrames run n+1 steps when the rate is 0, which is the shape of HF2.

TOOL 7 session-run REBUILT on a new tools/experience/lib/capabilities.mjs which classifies the WHOLE live surface into 10 capability classes and FAILS CLOSED on anything unclassified. Profiles now refuse CAPABILITIES; the method list is derived from the live surface at install time. first-hour refuses 107 of 325 methods, against RI-EXP01's 6 literal names (which are asserted to be a subset on every run, so the item's list is a lower bound that cannot be dropped).

session-run RED+GREEN on the running engine: CONTROL spawnNPC really puts an NPC in the world (listNPCs 0 -> 1) before the profile; after install all ten of TOOL-COVERAGE-R2 §8's bypasses (spawnNPC, spawnEncounter, spawnCivilian, spawnGuard, spawnProp, restoreState, travelRide, boardTravel, setTravelMark, __breakTravelFence) are refused and recorded, and the ENTITY-SIDE check shows listNPCs 1 -> 1 across a refused spawnNPC. GREEN: listEntities/getPlayerStats/getUIState/stepFrames/queueInputs still work. --self-test 14/14.

THE FAIL-CLOSED FUSE FIRED FOR REAL, unprompted: the harness surface grew 319 -> 325 methods DURING this pass and session-run --self-test REFUSED, naming explainDisposition, questDef and setFactionStanding as unclassified-and-therefore-refused. Classified and re-run 14/14. That is the exact failure mode round 2 had (six names against a growing surface) demonstrated to be closed.
